subject: HEALTH
title: Health Education 8
description: A skills-based grade 8 health course that builds on Health 7 with deeper study of resilience, suicide prevention and the effects of social media on mental health; energy balance, body image and evaluating supplements; comprehensive sexual health aligned with the California Healthy Youth Act (reproduction, abstinence and medically accurate prevention, HIV/STIs, gender identity and respect, healthy relationships and consent, human trafficking and sextortion awareness); opioids, naloxone, addiction and recovery; CPR and violence prevention; and consumer and community health. Sexual health lessons (weeks 11-18) are designed for parent preview, and parents may opt their student out under CA Education Code 51938; an alternative assignment is provided.
framework: 2008 California Health Education Content Standards (Grades 7–8); 2019 CA Health Education Framework; California Healthy Youth Act (Ed. Code 51930–51939)

standards.H-8.1.2.M: Describe resilience, self-esteem and protective factors and how they support mental health.
standards.H-8.1.4.M: Describe grief and loss and healthy ways to cope.
standards.H-8.1.5.M: Identify warning signs of suicide and self-harm, myths and facts, and immediate steps for getting help (including the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline).
standards.H-8.2.1.M: Analyze how social media and technology use influence mood, self-image, sleep and relationships.
standards.H-8.3.1.M: Access valid mental health resources in the community, at school and online.
standards.H-8.6.1.M: Set a goal to strengthen a mental or emotional health skill and monitor progress.
standards.H-8.8.1.M: Advocate for reducing stigma around mental illness and for help-seeking.
standards.H-8.1.2.N: Explain energy balance and the nutritional needs of active, growing adolescents.
standards.H-8.1.5.N: Describe the signs, health risks and treatment of eating disorders and disordered eating.
standards.H-8.2.2.N: Analyze how media, culture and peers influence body image and food choices.
standards.H-8.3.2.N: Evaluate sports supplements, energy drinks and diet products using valid information.
standards.H-8.7.2.N: Plan and prepare healthy, budget-friendly meals and snacks; describe food insecurity and community food resources.
standards.H-8.1.2.G: Describe the human reproductive process, including fertilization, pregnancy and fetal development (CHYA; parent opt-out).
standards.H-8.1.3.G: Explain that abstinence is the only certain way to prevent pregnancy and STIs, and describe the effectiveness of FDA-approved methods of preventing pregnancy and STIs, medically accurate and age-appropriate (CHYA; parent opt-out).
standards.H-8.1.5.G: Describe how HIV and other sexually transmitted infections are transmitted, prevented, tested for and treated (CHYA; parent opt-out).
standards.H-8.1.6.G: Describe gender identity, gender expression and sexual orientation and the importance of treating all people with dignity and respect (CHYA).
standards.H-8.1.8.G: Describe characteristics of healthy, unhealthy and abusive dating relationships and the meaning of affirmative consent.
standards.H-8.2.1.G: Analyze influences of media, peers and culture on beliefs about relationships and sexuality.
standards.H-8.3.2.G: Identify trusted adults and valid local resources for reproductive health care and relationship support, including minors' rights to confidential services in California.
standards.H-8.4.2.G: Demonstrate refusal, negotiation and help-seeking communication in relationship situations.
standards.H-8.5.1.G: Use a decision-making model to evaluate the consequences of sexual activity and choose healthy behaviors consistent with family values.
standards.H-8.1.9.G: Recognize warning signs of human trafficking and sexual exploitation (including sextortion) and how to seek help.
standards.H-8.1.2.A: Explain the effects of alcohol on the developing brain, blood alcohol concentration and impaired judgment, including driving under the influence.
standards.H-8.1.4.A: Describe opioids, fentanyl, overdose signs and how naloxone is used to reverse an opioid overdose.
standards.H-8.1.5.A: Describe the misuse of prescription stimulants, inhalants, caffeine and energy drinks and high-potency cannabis products.
standards.H-8.1.7.A: Describe addiction as a treatable disease and the stages of treatment and recovery.
standards.H-8.2.2.A: Analyze tobacco, vaping, alcohol and cannabis industry marketing tactics aimed at youth.
standards.H-8.4.1.A: Demonstrate how to help a friend who may be using substances and how to get adult help.
standards.H-8.5.2.A: Explain California laws and consequences related to alcohol, tobacco and drug possession and use by minors.
standards.H-8.1.3.S: Explain hands-only CPR, AED use and choking response for teens and adults.
standards.H-8.1.4.S: Describe risk factors for and prevention of dating violence, sexual harassment and assault.
standards.H-8.1.6.S: Describe safety risks of distracted walking, cycling and riding with impaired or distracted drivers.
standards.H-8.1.8.S: Describe safe storage of firearms and steps to take if a weapon is seen or a threat is heard.
standards.H-8.4.1.S: Demonstrate strategies to de-escalate conflict and report threats or harassment.
standards.H-8.7.2.S: Practice responding to emergencies, including heat illness, water emergencies and wildfire smoke.
standards.H-8.1.2.P: Explain risk factors for chronic diseases (heart disease, diabetes, cancer, asthma) and how behavior affects risk.
standards.H-8.2.1.P: Analyze how advertising and health claims influence the purchase of health products and services.
standards.H-8.3.2.P: Evaluate health products, services and online health information for validity as a responsible consumer.
standards.H-8.1.7.P: Describe the role of public health agencies and health careers in protecting community health.
standards.H-8.6.1.P: Develop a personal health plan for the transition to high school that addresses multiple areas of health.
standards.H-8.8.2.P: Plan and carry out a health advocacy campaign that influences others to make healthy choices.

resources.name: NIDA for Teens / Parents & Educators
resources.note: Science-based facts on drugs, opioids and addiction

units.title: Mental, Emotional and Social Health: Resilience and Help-Seeking
units.big_idea: Resilience, healthy tech habits and knowing how to get help protect mental health; mental illness is treatable.

units.title: Nutrition, Body Image and Performance
units.big_idea: A growing body needs energy balance; media can distort body image, and valid information protects against harmful products.

units.title: Growth, Development and Sexual Health (CA Healthy Youth Act)
units.big_idea: Accurate information, respect for all people, clear boundaries and trusted adults support healthy relationships and decisions. Parents may opt their student out of sexual health lessons (Ed. Code 51938).

units.title: Alcohol, Tobacco and Other Drugs: Beyond the Basics
units.big_idea: Addiction is a treatable disease; recognizing marketing, overdose signs and the law empowers safe choices and helping others.

units.title: Injury Prevention, Violence Prevention and Emergency Response
units.big_idea: Knowing how to respond in an emergency and how to prevent violence can save lives.

units.title: Personal, Consumer and Community Health
units.big_idea: Smart health consumers, public health systems and personal plans prevent disease across a lifetime.

days.title: Grade 7 recap
days.work: Review the stress-coping strategies from grade 7 and rate how often you use each.

days.title: Resilience

days.title: Protective factors
days.work: Map your protective factors (people, activities, strengths) on a support web.

days.title: Growth mindset
days.work: Rewrite five fixed-mindset statements as growth-mindset statements.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a short reflection on a setback you overcame and which protective factors helped.

weeks.topic: Technology, social media and mental health
objectives: Analyze how social media affects mood and sleep

days.title: Screen audit
days.work: Record your screen time by app for two days using device settings or a log.

days.title: Algorithms
days.work: Learn how feeds are designed to keep users scrolling; analyze one platform's features.

days.title: Comparison
days.work: Discuss how edited images and highlight reels affect self-image; find two examples of filtered vs. real photos.

days.title: Sleep link
days.work: Compare screen time before bed to your sleep log from PE and identify a pattern.

days.title: Goal
days.work: Write a SMART tech-balance goal and get a parent signature.

objectives: Distinguish mental health from mental illness

days.title: Continuum

days.title: Common conditions

days.title: Stigma

days.title: Treatment
days.work: Learn what counselors, psychologists and psychiatrists do and how to access them.

days.title: Check
days.work: Create a one-page anti-stigma infographic.

days.title: Facts and myths
days.work: Sort myth/fact cards about suicide (e.g., asking about suicide does not plant the idea).

days.title: Warning signs
days.work: Identify verbal, behavioral and situational warning signs.

days.title: Ask-Listen-Tell
days.work: Practice with a parent how to ask a friend directly, listen and tell a trusted adult.

days.title: Resources
days.work: Save 988 and the Crisis Text Line in your phone and list three trusted adults.

days.title: Check
days.work: Complete a wallet card with warning signs and help steps; discuss feelings with a parent.

materials: picture book or article on grief

days.title: Kinds of loss
days.work: List types of loss (death, moving, divorce, friendship ending, pet) and how each may feel.

days.title: Grief reactions
days.work: Learn that grief is not linear and identify common physical and emotional reactions.

days.title: Supporting others

days.title: Check

days.title: Share
days.work: Share the PSA with family and gather feedback.

days.title: Goal check

days.title: Unit test
days.work: Take a unit test on resilience, mental illness, warning signs and resources.

days.work: Learn how calories in and out relate to growth; calculate a sample MyPlate Plan for your age and activity.

days.title: Key nutrients
days.work: Research calcium, iron and vitamin D needs during adolescence and list three food sources each.

days.title: Food log
days.work: Log one day of meals and compare with your MyPlate Plan.

days.title: Fix it

days.title: Check

weeks.topic: Body image, media and eating disorders
objectives: Analyze media influences on body image
Recognize signs of eating disorders and how to get help

days.title: Media lens
days.work: Analyze three ads or posts for unrealistic body messages and photo editing.

days.title: Body image
days.work: Discuss influences on body image (family, peers, culture, sports) and write positive self-talk statements.

days.title: Eating disorders
days.work: Learn warning signs and health risks of anorexia, bulimia and binge eating disorder.

days.title: Getting help
days.work: Practice telling a trusted adult about concern for a friend and list where to find help.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a media-literacy response to one ad, explaining its message and a healthier counter-message.

weeks.topic: Supplements, energy drinks and diet claims
objectives: Explain risks of energy drinks for teens

days.title: Label study
days.work: Compare caffeine and sugar in three energy drinks with the recommended limit for teens.

days.title: Supplement claims
days.work: Evaluate two protein or 'fat-burner' supplement ads with a claim-checking checklist.

days.title: Regulation
days.work: Learn how FDA regulation differs for supplements and medicines.

days.work: Compare marketing claims with the evidence-based fuel plan from PE.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a consumer review debunking or supporting one product claim with sources.

objectives: Plan and cook a healthy budget meal
Describe food insecurity and community resources

days.title: Unit price
days.work: Compare unit prices of three staple foods in a grocery ad to find the best value.

days.title: Plan
days.work: Plan a balanced dinner for four under a set budget.

days.title: Cook
days.work: Cook the meal with a parent using food-safety practices from grade 7.

days.title: Food security
days.work: Learn about food insecurity in California and local food banks and CalFresh.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Take the nutrition unit test and reflect on the meal you made.

weeks.assessment: Meal plan, cooking and unit test.

weeks.topic: Introduction: sexual health, values and trusted adults
objectives: Explain the purpose of CHYA instruction and family opt-out
Identify trusted adults and valid sources

days.title: Family preview
days.work: Parent and student preview the unit, discuss family values and decide on any opt-out. (Sexual health lesson: parents may opt out under CA Ed. Code 51938; parent previews materials.)

days.title: Grade 7 recap
days.work: Review puberty, hormones and reproductive anatomy from grade 7 with a labeling warm-up.

days.title: Influences
days.work: Analyze how TV, music and social media portray relationships and sexuality versus reality.

days.title: Valid sources
days.work: Compare one reliable (e.g., KidsHealth) and one unreliable website on a sexual health question.

days.title: Check
days.work: List three trusted adults and two valid resources; write a question box question for a parent.

objectives: Describe fertilization and stages of pregnancy
Explain the importance of prenatal care

days.title: Fertilization
days.work: Study a diagram of fertilization and implantation with parent guidance. (Sexual health lesson: parents may opt out under CA Ed. Code 51938; parent previews materials.)

days.title: Trimesters
days.work: Create a timeline of fetal development across three trimesters.

days.title: Prenatal care
days.work: Explain how nutrition, alcohol, tobacco and prenatal checkups affect a developing baby.

days.title: Responsibilities
days.work: Interview a parent about the responsibilities and costs of raising a child.

days.title: Check
days.work: Complete a fetal development timeline quiz.

objectives: Explain abstinence as the only 100% effective method
Describe effectiveness of FDA-approved methods in medically accurate, age-appropriate terms

days.title: Abstinence
days.work: Discuss why abstinence is the only certain way to avoid pregnancy and STIs and reasons teens choose it. (Sexual health lesson: parents may opt out under CA Ed. Code 51938; parent previews materials.)

days.title: Methods overview
days.work: Review a chart comparing the effectiveness of FDA-approved methods (no demonstrations).

days.title: Decision model
days.work: Apply a decision-making model to a scenario about waiting to have sex.

days.title: Family talk
days.work: Discuss family values about relationships and decisions with a parent.

days.title: Check
days.work: Answer short-response questions on abstinence and method effectiveness.

objectives: Describe transmission and prevention of HIV and other STIs

days.title: Transmission
days.work: Learn how HIV and common STIs are and are not transmitted using a fact/myth sort. (Sexual health lesson: parents may opt out under CA Ed. Code 51938; parent previews materials.)

days.title: Symptoms
days.work: Learn that many STIs have no symptoms and why testing matters.

days.title: Prevention and treatment
days.work: Describe prevention strategies and that HIV is treatable with medicine.

days.title: Rights and resources
days.work: Learn California minors' rights to confidential STI testing and find a local clinic.

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a quiz on STI and HIV transmission, prevention and testing.

weeks.topic: Gender identity, sexual orientation and respect
objectives: Define gender identity, gender expression and sexual orientation

days.title: Vocabulary
days.work: Define gender identity, gender expression and sexual orientation using a medically accurate glossary; discuss with a parent.

days.title: Stereotypes
days.work: Identify gender stereotypes in ads, toys and media and how they limit people.

days.title: Respect
days.work: Discuss how bullying based on identity harms mental health and practice upstander responses.

days.title: Support
days.work: Identify supportive resources and trusted adults for any teen with questions.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a paragraph on how to treat all people with dignity and respect.

objectives: Compare healthy, unhealthy and abusive relationships

days.title: Spectrum
days.work: Sort relationship behaviors onto a healthy-unhealthy-abusive spectrum.

days.title: Red flags
days.work: Identify digital red flags such as checking phones, demanding passwords and constant texting.

days.title: Affirmative consent
days.work: Learn that consent must be clear, ongoing and can be withdrawn; analyze scenarios (non-sexual and sexual examples, age-appropriate).

days.title: Communication
days.work: Practice refusal and negotiation phrases with a parent.

days.title: Check
days.work: Analyze a short story's relationship and identify healthy and unhealthy behaviors.

weeks.topic: Human trafficking, sextortion and online exploitation
objectives: Recognize recruitment tactics and warning signs
materials: CA DOJ or NCMEC Take It Down information

days.title: What is trafficking
days.work: Learn what human trafficking is and that it happens in California, often by someone the victim knows.

days.title: Grooming
days.work: Identify grooming and recruitment tactics online and in person (gifts, secrecy, isolation).

days.title: Sextortion
days.work: Learn what sextortion is, that it is never the victim's fault, and steps: stop, don't pay, save evidence, tell an adult, use NCMEC Take It Down.

days.title: Help
days.work: Role-play telling a trusted adult and list the National Human Trafficking Hotline.

days.title: Check
days.work: Create a safety tip card for younger teens.

weeks.topic: Sexual health review and decision making

days.title: Scenarios
days.work: Apply the decision-making model to three relationship scenarios.

days.title: Future goals
days.work: Write how decisions now affect future goals (school, sports, career).

days.title: Communication
days.work: Write a script for talking to a parent about a relationship question.

days.title: Review
days.work: Review vocabulary and concepts from the unit with flashcards.

days.title: Unit test
days.work: Take the unit test (alternative assignment on puberty, hygiene and relationships for opted-out students).

objectives: Describe CA laws for minors and DUI

days.title: Grade 7 recap
days.work: Review alcohol's effects on the body from grade 7 with a quick quiz.

days.title: BAC
days.work: Learn factors affecting BAC (size, sex, food, time) and why the teen brain is more vulnerable.

days.title: Impairment
days.work: Try a coordination task while 'impaired' with drunk-buster-style challenges (walking a line while counting backward).

days.title: The law
days.work: Learn California's zero-tolerance law for drivers under 21 and social host liability.

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a plan for what to do if a ride's driver has been drinking.

objectives: Identify signs of an opioid overdose

days.title: Opioids
days.work: Learn how opioids affect breathing and why fentanyl in counterfeit pills is deadly.

days.title: Overdose signs
days.work: Identify overdose signs (pinpoint pupils, slow breathing, unresponsive).

days.title: Naloxone
days.work: Watch a naloxone nasal-spray training video and practice the steps on a model.

days.title: Good Samaritan
days.work: Learn California's Good Samaritan law that protects people who call 911.

days.title: Check
days.work: Sequence the steps for responding to a suspected overdose.

weeks.topic: Stimulants, inhalants, caffeine and cannabis potency
objectives: Describe risks of misused prescription stimulants and inhalants
Compare cannabis potency today and past

days.title: Prescription stimulants
days.work: Learn why 'study drugs' are risky when misused and the law on sharing prescriptions.

days.title: Inhalants
days.work: Learn how household inhalants damage the brain and can cause sudden death.

days.title: Caffeine
days.work: Calculate your weekly caffeine intake and compare with recommended limits.

days.title: Cannabis potency
days.work: Compare THC potency of modern vapes and edibles with the past and explain risks to teen brains.

days.title: Check
days.work: Complete a drug-facts chart with effects, risks and laws.

materials: vape, alcohol or cannabis ads (online examples)

days.title: Tactics
days.work: Identify marketing tactics (flavors, influencers, packaging, sponsorships) aimed at youth.

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Analyze two ads using a media-literacy checklist.

days.title: Industry
days.work: Learn about California's flavored tobacco ban and why it passed.

days.title: Counter-ad
days.work: Design a counter-ad that exposes one tactic.

days.title: Check
days.work: Present the counter-ad to a parent and explain the tactic.

objectives: Explain addiction as a treatable disease

days.title: Brain changes
days.work: Review how dopamine and tolerance lead to addiction.

days.title: Disease model

days.title: Treatment
days.work: Research types of treatment (counseling, medication, support groups).

days.title: Recovery stories

days.title: Check
days.work: Write a paragraph explaining addiction to a younger student.

weeks.topic: Helping a friend and unit assessment
objectives: Help a friend who is using substances

days.title: Getting help

days.title: Review
days.work: Review unit concepts with a jeopardy-style game.

days.title: Unit test
days.work: Take the unit test on alcohol, opioids, other drugs, marketing and addiction.

objectives: Use an AED and respond to choking

days.title: Check-call-care
days.work: Review emergency steps and practice a 911 call script.

days.title: Hands-only CPR
days.work: Practice compressions at 100-120 per minute on a pillow to a song beat.

days.title: AED
days.work: Watch an AED demonstration and sequence the steps.

days.title: Choking
days.work: Practice the universal choking sign and abdominal thrust positioning (no real thrusts).

days.title: Check
days.work: Complete a CPR scenario walk-through while a parent checks steps.

weeks.topic: Heat, water and wildfire smoke emergencies
objectives: Respond to water emergencies and poor air quality

days.title: Heat illness
days.work: Compare heat exhaustion and heat stroke and first aid for each.

days.title: Water rescue
days.work: Learn reach-throw-don't go and rip current escape.

days.title: Air quality
days.work: Check the AQI on AirNow and learn when to limit outdoor activity.

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a scenario quiz on heat, water and smoke emergencies.

weeks.topic: Distracted walking, biking and safe rides

days.work: Analyze teen pedestrian and cyclist injury data.

days.title: Distraction test

days.title: Blind spots
days.work: Learn vehicle blind spots and how to be visible.

days.title: Safe rides
days.work: Discuss refusing rides with distracted or impaired drivers and a family code word.

days.title: Harassment
days.work: Define sexual harassment and identify examples in person and online.

days.work: Write a reflection on how you would support a friend.

materials: Sandy Hook Promise Say Something resources
